ideas: What the tradition is and when it happens
Your own memories of taking part
Why it still matters to you today

phrases.phrase: passed down from generation to generation

phrases.meaning: continue a custom so it doesn't disappear

model: The tradition I value most is Tet, the Lunar New Year, and especially the custom of visiting our grandparents' house on the first day. Although I live in Ho Chi Minh City now, I always fly back to my hometown in Nam Dinh for it. The house is cleaned and decorated for days beforehand, and special food like banh chung is made by my aunts, which usually takes a whole night to boil. On the first morning, the whole family gathers in front of the ancestral altar. We burn incense and pay respect to our ancestors, and then the children are given lucky money in red envelopes. When I was a kid, I honestly only cared about the envelopes. But now it's become a real family reunion for me, because it's the only time all my cousins are in one place. While it's true that the celebration is quite tiring, with endless visits to neighbours and relatives, I've never wanted to skip it. These customs have been passed down from generation to generation, and they give me a strong sense of belonging. Despite the fact that many young people now travel abroad during Tet instead, I really hope my generation will keep the tradition alive. Last year I was asked by my grandmother to learn how to wrap banh chung properly, and I felt quite proud that she trusted me with it.
